spec.title: Cap each tool result to a share of the working budget; answer from notes after back-to-back compactions
spec.problem:
Live: the 9B explorer (16K window, about 24.7K characters of working budget) read two whole files that overflowed the budget by themselves, compacted, re-read them, and compacted again every step until it ran out of steps. In agent.py, the Agent should expose `result_chars`, the most characters one tool result may take: a quarter of its history budget, at least 2,000. A longer result is cut at a line boundary; for numbered read_file output (lines like `   12| text`) it ends with a note naming where to continue, in the form `start_line=<next line>`, and the recorded read range (`agent.reads[call_id]`, a tuple whose third item is the last line) ends at the last line shown. If the agent has to compact on two consecutive steps, it is stuck: that step becomes its last step (only the finish tool is offered, named in tool_choice).

Environment: commands already run inside an OS sandbox here, and macOS cannot nest one, so tests that use the sandbox (tests/test_gates.py, test_mining.py, test_review_findings.py, test_tools_sandbox.py, test_workflow.py) fail in this environment whatever the change. The test command runs the hermetic test files only (test_agent, test_context, test_interfaces, test_publish, test_repomap); put new tests there.
acceptance_criteria: A tool result longer than agent.result_chars is cut to about that size at a line boundary
A cut read_file result names start_line=<next line> and its recorded read range ends at the last line shown
Compacting on two consecutive steps makes that step the last one, offering only the finish tool via a named tool_choice, so the run ends done instead of out of steps
